_notes: Four posts a week: Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Sunday. Stories on the days between.
Ground is one of: cocoa, rose, powder, cream, stripe. Never two of the same touching in the grid.
Entries with a 'tile' object are type led and are generated by npm run tiles. No camera needed.
Captions are linted. See tests/captions.test.mjs for what fails.

posts.headline: The line, alone on a dark ground
posts.caption:
Give the gift of sleep.

We are a small studio in Melbourne making beautiful rituals around going to bed: one gift box, four pieces, and your message written by hand. We open this month.

posts.headline: Silk, close enough to see the weave
posts.shoot: Pillowcase folded in thirds, raking side light, cream ground. Sell the material before the product.
posts.caption:
Grade 6A mulberry silk at 22 momme. Heavy enough to drape properly, and heavy enough to survive being washed for years.

Everything in the box had to feel like this against a warm cheek at 2am.

posts.headline: Hands smoothing a pillowcase
posts.shoot: One shot. No talking, no trending audio, ambient room sound. Cover styled as a clay rose type tile so the grid holds.
posts.caption: The last thing you do before the light goes off.

posts.headline: Waitlist open
posts.caption: The list is open, link in bio. First boxes leave Melbourne this month.

weeks.note: Reveal. The Monday hero here is the image that will run as your ad and your homepage banner.

posts.headline: Closed, ribbon tied, overhead
posts.shoot: Shoot this one properly. It is the ad, the banner and the grid anchor. Straight overhead, powder ground, rose ribbon.
posts.caption:
The Gift of Sleep Box. For the person who needs absolutely nothing except a good night's sleep.

$149, free shipping Australia wide, packed by hand in Fitzroy.

posts.headline: One item per slide
posts.shoot: Each on a different ground: cocoa, powder, cream, rose. Item name in display type. No prices on the slides. Final slide is the ritual card on the tissue.
posts.caption:
Swipe for everything inside.

Silk sleep mask. Silk pillowcase, cut from the same run. An AM / PM journal for either end of the day. A lavender sleep wrap with a good weight to it. The ritual card on top, and your message, written by hand.

posts.headline: Unboxing in real time
posts.shoot: Ribbon pull, tissue open, lid off, one item lifted out. No sped up footage, no captions on screen.
posts.caption: What arrives at their door.

posts.headline: Instead of flowers
posts.shoot: Nothing. Generated tile. Use this line on the box sleeve too so print and feed match.
posts.caption:
Not a hamper. Not a candle with a bow on it. Four pieces that were chosen against each other, and a card with your words on it.

Flowers last a week. The box stays on the bedside table.

weeks.note: Changed again with the brand: rituals are the editorial spine now. Content that is useful on its own, with the pieces underneath it.

posts.headline: Tonight, try this
posts.caption:
The 15 minute night reset.

Phone down, somewhere else. Lights low. Write down what is still in your head. Put your mask on. Goodnight.

The whole ritual is on the site, and it works with whatever you already own.

posts.headline: The journal, open, lamp on
posts.shoot: AM / PM journal open on a bedside table, pen across it, one warm lamp. The PM page half filled with anything illegible.
posts.caption:
A page for the end of the day and a page for the start of the next one.

The PM page is for whatever is still circling. It does not have to read well. It has to be out of your head and on the page.

posts.headline: The wind down, real time
posts.shoot: Lamp on, journal closed, mask picked up, light off. Ambient sound, no talking, no captions on screen.
posts.caption: The last hour, with nothing that glows in it.

posts.headline: Give the most important thing
posts.caption:
Give the most important thing.

The box is $149. The silk mask on its own is $49. Both leave Melbourne the same afternoon if you order before the cut-off.

evergreen._note: A bank to drop into any week when a shoot slips or a Sunday arrives and nothing is ready. All type led, so none of them need a camera. Rotate rather than repeat inside a month.

posts.caption:
Two of us, one bench, about forty boxes on a good weekday.

Everything goes in the same order every time: tissue, pillowcase, wrap, journal, mask, then the ritual card on top so it is the first thing under the lid. Your card goes in last, in pen.

Your message, in pen, on a printed card, before the lid goes on.

Up to 250 characters and we write it exactly as you type it, line breaks and all. We will quietly fix an obvious typo in a name and leave the rest alone.

The thing you send when flowers feel like a shrug.

Four pieces, a ritual card and your words in pen, in a box that stays on the bedside table long after a bunch would have gone in the bin.

tile.text: The last thing before the light goes off

posts.caption:
Lamp, journal, mask, light off. In that order, because the mask goes on last.

What the ritual is matters far less than that it never changes.

No pricing on the outside of the parcel either, so it can go straight to them.

Put their address at checkout and your words on the card. That is the whole thing.

Most silk in gift sets is 16 momme, and it is silk on the front with polyester behind.

Ours is 22 momme on both faces, cut from one run so the mask and the pillowcase match exactly. It is the difference you feel in a year, not on day one.
